gabarito.reason:
Util.md5Hex (Util.java:1000) has two kinds of caller, and neither can move to SHA-256. (1) Util.getRestUrl (Util.java:397-404) uses it for Subsonic token authentication: it sends s=<random salt> and t=md5Hex(password + salt). The Subsonic/Madsonic/Airsonic REST API fixes this formula. The server recomputes MD5(password + salt) and compares the result, so a SHA-256 token would be rejected and every user on a token-capable server would be locked out. (2) FileUtil (lines 271, 274, 296, 323, 350) uses it to build cache file names for album art, playlist/podcast covers, avatars and misc images (md5Hex(path/username/url) + ".jpeg"). That is a non-security name hash. Changing the algorithm would orphan every existing cached image on users' devices for no security gain. In neither case is MD5 doing work that collision or preimage resistance would protect: the token is protocol-mandated, and the file names are only identifiers. The real weaknesses of token auth (MD5 of the password, a cleartext password needed on the server) are properties of the Subsonic protocol, so this app cannot fix them on its own. The rule's suggested fix of swapping in SHA-256 is wrong here, so a PR cannot be accepted. An issue asking for SHA-256 would only point maintainers at a change that breaks authentication. The finding is a false positive for this code, so nothing should be sent.

Second judge: Util.md5Hex computes lowercase hexadecimal MD5 over UTF-8 input. Its security-sensitive caller, getRestUrl, sends t=MD5(password + salt) with s=salt for Subsonic token authentication. ServerInfo.canUseToken enables this for stock Subsonic REST versions >=1.14 unless blocked. Replacing MD5 with SHA-256 would change the authentication protocol and cause server rejection; the repository provides no alternative digest negotiation. Other callers in FileUtil use MD5 solely for deterministic image-cache filenames, not security checks. No corrective algorithm-replacement PR is justified by this report. NO_ACTION is reasonable; an ISSUE is also acceptable if it explains the protocol constraint and authentication limitation without claiming that a client-only SHA substitution fixes it.
must_not_break: Subsonic REST token authentication: t must stay hex(MD5(password + salt)), sent with s=salt, or servers (Subsonic, Airsonic, Navidrome, Madsonic, etc.) will reject every request when ServerInfo.canUseToken is true
The cached token/salt pairs in Util.getRestUrl and the server's matching recomputation

Existing on-disk image cache file names (album art, avatars, playlist/podcast covers, misc URL images) built from md5Hex(...) + ".jpeg" in FileUtil; changing the hash orphans the cached files and forces re-downloads
Compatibility with older servers that use the legacy p=enc: path and with token-capable servers, as chosen by ServerInfo

Preserve the server-compatible token calculation: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from MD5 of UTF-8(password + salt), paired with the corresponding s parameter. Substituting SHA-2 would break token authentication and authenticated requests.

Preserve server capability and blocked-token handling, including the existing enc:-prefixed UTF-8 hexadecimal password fallback for setups without token authentication. Disabling tokens merely to avoid MD5 would transmit the reversibly encoded password instead.

Preserve access to existing MD5-named .jpeg files for playlist and podcast artwork, album-directory artwork, avatars, and URL-based miscellaneous images, including offline artwork and the existing migration from hashed album artwork to the album directory. Changing filenames without compatible lookup or migration would orphan cached images.
